steps.label: Why and How We Compress
steps.content:
Data Storage and Compression

Why and How We Compress

Year 10, 1.3 L3 · Compression · 30 minutes

  • Concept: Why files are compressed, and what that changes.
  • Challenges: Make an image and a sound smaller the lossy way, and see what is lost.
  • Exam link: Seven real Cambridge compression questions.
  • Also today: Lossless compression of text and images.

steps.label: Why Compress a File?
steps.content:
Why Compress a File?

Compression reduces the size of a file. A smaller file has three effects:

  • Less storage space is needed to keep it.
  • Less bandwidth is needed to send it across a network.
  • Shorter transmission time: it uploads, downloads or emails faster.

There are two methods: lossy permanently removes data, lossless removes none.

Exam Question: Compressing Before Emailing (1 of 2)

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, February/March 2022, Question 2(c). Nadia compresses the digital image file before emailing it to a friend.

items.prompt: (c)(i) State what is meant by data compression.
items.modelAnswer: Reducing the size of a file.

steps.label: Exam Question: Compressing Before Emailing (2 of 2)
steps.content:
Exam Question: Compressing Before Emailing (2 of 2)

Continued. Nadia compresses the digital image file before emailing it to a friend.

items.prompt: (c)(ii) Explain why Nadia compresses the digital image file before emailing it.
items.modelAnswer: Any two of: the smaller file takes less time to send (and for her friend to download); it uses less bandwidth; it may be under the email service's attachment size limit, so it can be sent at all; it takes up less storage space in both mailboxes.

steps.label: Lossy: Permanently Removing Data
steps.content:
Lossy: Permanently Removing Data

Lossy compression makes a file smaller by permanently removing data. The removed data can never be put back. It works by lowering the settings in the file size formula:

  • Images: reduce the resolution (fewer pixels) or reduce the colour depth (fewer bits per pixel).
  • Sound: reduce the sample rate (fewer samples per second) or reduce the sample resolution (fewer bits per sample).
  • Halving any one setting halves the file size, because it is one of the numbers being multiplied.

steps.label: Exam Question: Lossy Thumbnails
steps.content:
Exam Question: Lossy Thumbnails

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, February/March 2021, Question 2(a). Gurdeep takes high definition photographs. Users of her website can view thumbnails, small versions of the photographs. She compresses the photographs with lossy compression to create the thumbnails.

items.prompt: (a) Describe how lossy compression creates the thumbnails.
items.modelAnswer: Any three of: a compression algorithm is used; data is permanently removed from the photograph; the resolution is reduced, so there are fewer pixels; the colour depth can be reduced, so fewer bits are used for each pixel; detail that will not be noticed in a small thumbnail is removed; the file size is reduced.

steps.label: Lossless: Nothing Is Lost
steps.content:
Lossless: Nothing Is Lost

Lossless compression reduces the file size without permanently losing any data. Decompressing it rebuilds the original exactly.

  • Run length encoding (RLE) stores each run of repeated data once, with a count: WWWWWBBB becomes 5W 3B.
  • It works on text as well as images: AAAABBBCC becomes 4A 3B 2C.
  • Other lossless methods find repeating patterns in the data and index them, so each pattern is stored only once.
  • Use lossless when every bit matters: text, program files, or an image that must stay exact.

steps.label: Exam Question: Which Type?
steps.content:
Exam Question: Which Type?

Based on Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2022, Question 1(a)(ii) and 0478/13, June 2022, Question 6(d).

items.prompt: Jack has an MP3 file stored on his computer. Is it a lossy compressed file, a lossless compressed file, or not a compressed file?
options: It depends on how long the track is
items.explain: MP3 removes sound data a listener is unlikely to notice, so it is lossy.

items.prompt: Frida compresses a document. The algorithm recognises repeating patterns in the data and indexes them. No data is permanently removed. Which type of compression is this?
items.explain: No data is permanently removed, which is exactly what lossless means.

steps.label: Exam Question: Explain Lossless
steps.content:
Exam Question: Explain Lossless

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2025, Question 2(d). A student has an image file stored on their computer, with a colour depth of 32 bits. The student uses lossless compression to compress the image file.

items.prompt: (d) Explain how the image file is compressed using lossless compression.
items.modelAnswer: Any three of: a compression algorithm is used, such as run length encoding (RLE); it finds runs of repeated, identical pixels (colours); each run is stored once as the number of repeats and the colour; so the file size is reduced; no data is permanently removed, so the original image can be rebuilt exactly.

steps.label: Exam Question: Compressing a Text File
steps.content:
Exam Question: Compressing a Text File

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2026, Question 1(c)(iii). The computer uses the ASCII character set for a text file. The text file needs to be compressed.

items.prompt: (c)(iii) Identify the most appropriate type of compression for the text file. Justify your choice.
items.modelAnswer: Compression type: lossless. Justification, any three of: no data is permanently removed; the text file can be decompressed to exactly the original; if characters were removed the text would not make sense, or its meaning would change; every character is needed, so none can be lost; a method such as RLE or indexing repeated words can still reduce the file size.
